summary.verdict: INCONCLUSIVE: a group has fewer than 30 events

rows.reason: Gold Bar production miss and higher AISC were already disclosed, and the -2.2% move looks like a fair reaction. Los Azules financing and exploration updates are incremental, so I have no clear view.

The -12.6% drop already prices in the weak quarter, which included one-offs (CAD 45M insurance, CAD 54.7M capacity-utilization benefit), a Q3 volume trough (shipments down 10-20%), a loss of the submarine MOU, and a cash burn funded by CAD 124.5M of loan draws. Offsetting items are the CAD 200M tax refund, rising realized prices and plate demand, and Unit 2 start-up. The balance looks fairly priced.

Positive news (new orders priced more than 15% higher, US volume +29%, needle coke tightening, cost guidance held) was largely priced in by the +9.7% move, and the ATM equity program, heavy cash burn and flat 2Q pricing offset it.

Solid Q2 beat on lower weather losses and prior-year reserve releases, with premiums shrinking (-4%), a softening market, and an elevated expense ratio; this looks largely priced into the modest +2.2% move, so no clear unreflected edge.

Mixed quarter (GAAP loss, EAD down to $0.15 vs $0.21, book value down 3%) offset by strong mortgage banking volume, new JVs and legacy wind-down on track; the -5.3% move looks roughly fair, so no clear unpriced information.
Guidance midpoint held, EBITDA flat year over year, and the record FCF was flagged as timing; the +4.6% move already reflects the modest positives (deleveraging, H2 ramp on track).

The new dividend, the capex peak this year and Quintillion closing this year are real positives, but a +1.8% move likely already reflects them, and Q2 adjusted OIBDA fell 11% with margin pressure, so I see no clear unpriced edge.

A 13.6% drop looks like an overreaction to the soft Q3 margin guide (EBITDA flat to down against a big Q2 beat), which management attributes to transitory contract-pricing and cost lags; synergies are ahead of plan, leverage is falling, and transactional demand is strong.

Pre-revenue developer's first call after IPO: results and spending guidance were expected, with rising burn and a future financing need (debt first), and no new catalysts, so the -4.5% move looks fairly priced.

The call was mostly a recap of already-announced newbuild orders, charter backlog and dividend, with no new surprises. The -1.5% move looks fair, and the back-loaded newbuild capex is a modest offset to the strong coverage.

The +34.8% two-day jump already prices in the main positives (a record rocket-casting printer order, sequential Q3 growth guidance, printer sales up over 40%, and denture traction). Offsetting this are weak revenue growth of 1.4%, an EBITDA loss, a CEO exit, and a recent equity raise, so I see no clear unpriced edge.

Beat and raise (57% growth, 76.8% gross margin), with guidance that looks conservative (implied 45% H2 growth) and no revenue from the IPPS DRG change or the Q4 launches included, while the stock rose only 2%. Offsetting this, the cash burn and operating expenses are rising.

A 9.5% drop looks overdone for a clean first print: Q2 revenue beat by about $1.3M, 102% growth, 83% gross margin and FY guide of $54-56M. The likely negatives (only 4-5 territory adds a quarter in H2, a "measured" spend pace, heavy SG&A) were already known, and the November final CMS APC rule is a possible positive catalyst. The signal is modest, and post-IPO supply pressure could linger.

Strong quarter (EPS $0.83, carbon EBITDA $59M, $243M cash) but the -11% move likely reflects no 45Z monetization deal, no buyback, and Q3 margins "a touch below" Q2. The call adds nothing the price has missed, so I have no view.

Mixed call: Q3 organic sales returned to growth and the midpoint guide held, but narrowed guidance, a Q4 that depends on a heavy ramp, supply disruption and a modest gross margin cut roughly offset that; the rejected takeover bid was already public, so the -1.4% move looks fair.

Strong fundraising, FRE on track and guidance maintained were all in the release; the one negative (FY FRE margin modestly below target) is balanced by the PE fund markdowns being pre-disclosed, so the +1.8% move looks roughly fair.

The -11.3% drop already prices the main negatives (new impairments, book value down 4%, likely Q3 earnings drag, dividend risk). The loan-sale and turnover plan is a mixed signal, so I see no clear unpriced edge.

Broad-based commercial bookings recovery, a revenue and margin beat, and a guide implying a return to year-over-year growth by Q4 point to modest post-earnings drift. The +18.6% jump already prices in much of it, and leverage of 3.1x and weak federal book-to-bill of 0.8x limit the upside.

Core pawn metrics were very strong (PLO +31%, core gross profit +28%, EPS +47%) and the SMG buyout is complete, yet the stock fell 5.9% on scrap-margin normalization fears. Management already flagged scrap normalizing to 15-20%, so most of the drop looks priced in as a mild overreaction; a modest positive tilt, not strong.

Solid but expected quarter (NIM +9bp, clean credit, EPS up), offset by soft loan growth, higher expense guide and management signaling slower NIM gains; the -1.3% move looks fair, so there is no clear unreflected information.

Guidance raise (sales midpoint 11.7%, EBITDA 15.2%), 10% organic growth, a robust Q3 order file and a one-off Q2 margin hit expected to reverse suggest modest positive drift. The +29% move already prices most of this, and there are cost risks from oil and the Middle East.

FFO guidance was reaffirmed and management said office occupancy is now "binary" and could end slightly below the year-end range if large leases slip. That is a modest negative the -2.5% move likely already reflects. It is offset by $0.14 of signed-lease FFO upside and strong liquidity.

Solid beat-and-raise (revenue +4.5%, gross margin +140bp, Q3 guide above prior year, at-least-8% margin target), but the +6.1% move already prices most of it. Cash flow is negative and SG&A is deleveraging, so the net view is neutral.

The +38.7% jump is driven by the announced sale of the Colombia and Ecuador businesses. Management would not discuss the deal, and the operating results were modest, so the call adds little the price hasn't already absorbed.

Stock fell 6.4% despite a beat-and-raise (FFO guide up, record leasing, 99% occupancy, fixed-rate debt, dividend doubled); the drop looks like an overreaction to one-time Hawaii bad-debt reserve and noise, though high leverage (11.5x) limits upside.

Solid turnaround quarter (EBITDA +43%, leverage down to 5.4x, capex -70%) with guidance only maintained and a back-half-weighted EBITDA ramp, so the +7.7% move looks to have priced in the good news and the call adds little unreflected information.

Beat and raise (guidance up, buybacks resumed, leverage 1.7x, GMV turning positive) is offset by leasing write-offs of 8.4%, above the 6-8% annual range, and a back-half guide that assumes a fading 90-day-buyout tailwind. The 4.7% drop looks like a fair reaction to those credit worries, so I see no clear unreflected information.

In-line quarter with Q3 EBITDA guide of $92-98M (flat to slightly up), cost pressure from lube and O&M continuing; Valiant ahead of plan and strong FCF were positive but largely priced in by the +5.4% move.

The +14% move already reflects the positives: a $150M buyback, smaller TBV dilution (about 10% against 14% at announcement), and NIM guidance rising to the high 3.80s. Credit is the offset: NPLs nearly doubled to 1.64%, criticized loans rose to 7.7%, and charge-offs have been high for several periods. The call shows no clear unpriced information.

The -22.6% drop already reflects the SMB miss and the guide cut. Management's recovery claims (July best month since Q1, lenders back) are plausible but unproven, and insurance margins are pressured, so I see no clear unpriced edge.

The beat and raised guidance were largely driven by one-time tariff refunds, and the company is reinvesting most of them in marketing. Underlying trends are improving but still early, and the +14.8% move appears to already price this in.

Q3 guidance implies sequential growth (EPS $0.12-0.20 vs $0.11 in Q2; Production Enhancement margins rebounding to 12%) with offshore exploration momentum building, but the stock fell 3.2% and the Middle East and Russia-Ukraine risk keeps the edge small.

The 5.9% drop appears to price in the gross margin miss (38%, WildFireSat) and heavy cash burn, offset by reaffirmed guidance, over 85% contracted, a $12.4M legal award and near-term catalysts, but the Q4-weighted ramp is a real execution risk, so no clear edge.

Mixed call (REO writedown and a $28.6M C&I non-accrual with a $9.8M reserve, offset by NIM expansion, a raised NII guide, buybacks and a stable ~3.50% core NIM outlook); the roughly flat price move looks fair.

Strong beat and EBITDA guide raise, but the stock moved only +0.8%, and Q3 flat Lower 48 margin, negative Q3 FCF and 2027 capex at or above 2026 offset the positives, so I see no clear unpriced information.

The -9.6% drop looks like a reaction to the back-half-loaded growth guide (Q3 revenue of $475-485M implies a steep Q4 ramp) and to margin beats from lower bad debt and a shrinking insurance benefit. The call adds little the price hasn't already reflected.

Strong 23% revenue growth, a record $650M backlog and the expanded Honeywell APU distribution deal are offset by management saying Q2 included catch-up and is not the baseline. Operating cash flow was negative, inventory spend is rising, and landing gear has no visibility, so the -4.2% move looks fair.

Strong Q2 (comps +8%, EPS doubled, tariff refund help) but the +11.8% move already reflects it; flattering EPS is partly refunds and a lower tax rate, and fuel cost headwinds plus unchanged GM guidance temper the outlook.

Beat-and-raise quarter (rev +31.7%, US +141%, EBITDA positive, guide raised, FCF-positive path, ~25% 2027 growth) yet the stock fell 15.2%, which looks like an overreaction (maybe OUS growth of 4.4% or one-time costs), so I expect modest mean-reversion.

Raised guidance, margin expansion, a debt-reducing preferred refinancing, and a second-half ramp of data center, defense and medical wins not yet in results suggest modest unpriced upside after a flat +0.5% reaction. Share dilution and the still-pending term loan refinance temper the view.

Weak quarter (gross margin down, Jeeter ramp costs persisting, liquor and cannabis softness) was largely priced by the 11% drop, offset by net cash, buybacks and the Parallel deal, so no clear unreflected edge.

The guidance cut (FY EPS $1.60-2.00 vs $2.11 last year, Q3 loss guide, weak Lyons-brand-style assortment problem) was fully visible on the call and the -18% move seems to price it. Offsets are the debt paydown, falling capex and a December margin plan, but quarter-to-date comps are "down slightly", so I have no view.

The guidance cut (revenue to $330-340M from $350M), the billing-system collection shortfall and the continued cash burn were all disclosed on the call and are largely priced in by the 15.7% drop. Offsetting that, cash is large relative to the share count, a $106M tax refund is pending and buybacks continue, but the collection-rate recovery has no firm timeline.

The +27.7% move already prices in the critical-materials, Venezuela and trade-protection story. The underlying quarter is thin (adjusted EBITDA margin 3.5%, including a $5M one-off litigation gain) and the cost-cut targets are still vague.

Beat-and-raise (revenue above guidance, record EBITDA, FY guide raised, a second straight quarter of WAU growth) looks largely priced in by the +7.9% move. Offsetting points: Q3 EBITDA guide steps down from Q2, growth is mostly pricing, and branded marketing was cut 9%.

Stock fell ~30% on a guidance cut (revenue down about $40-50M, EPS down about $0.40 at midpoint) attributed to a roughly two-month delay in LOLA/line of credit launches, with credit worsening (net charge-offs 52% vs 43% of receivables) but recoveries and buybacks offsetting it. The drop looks like an overreaction, so I expect a modest rebound. Execution and bank-approval risk limit the score to +1.

Beat and guidance raise with a top-five bank win and Fiserv reseller are positive, but the +7.9% move already reflects them. The beat was helped by a one-time age-verification surge and check-renewal timing, and the Q4 guide implies a sequential step down, so the net information left is balanced.

Strong operating results (same-store NOI +16.9%, occupancy up, margin expansion, refinancing de-risked maturities, new COO, acquisition pipeline) against a -3.4% price move; modest positive drift likely, though the ATM equity issuance and lack of guidance limit conviction.

The -6.9% drop looks like a fair reaction to the revenue miss, weak education, a down Q1 and modest EBITDA guidance. The offsets (25% dividend raise, $183M buyback, 2-4% growth guide) were disclosed on the call and look priced in, so I see no clear unreflected information.

Q2 revenue and EBITDA hit the high end of guidance and Q3 guidance (about $265M revenue, $54M EBITDA) looks strong, with an accretive tuck-in deal and Asia subsea awards. The +12.6% move seems to have already priced most of this in, so I see no clear unpriced information.

Q3 EPS fell sharply on narrower spreads, but the call offers only unquantified promises of data-center shipment catch-up and a new price increase, and the +4.6% move already prices much of that relief.

Record revenue and cash flow, but about $2M was pull-ahead and Q3 guidance of $137-139M is sequentially lower. Margin gains depend on the manufacturing build-out (mid-year benefit, higher start-up costs). The +3.9% move already prices this in.

Strong beat-and-raise (Core FFO guidance up, SSNOI guide up, investment volume up) but the +1.5% move and ATM equity issuance, plus management flagging SSNOI moderation in H2, suggest it is largely priced in.

The +16.5% move already reflects the good news: $540M of new cloud contracts, NC-1 ramping to 40 MW by August, and exclusivity with lenders on NC-1 financing. The offsets are a delayed ramp and financing, only $56M of cash, a $15M net loss, and a CFO change, so I see no clear unpriced edge.
Big Modern Oral beat and raised pouch guidance were offset by adjusted EBITDA down 50%, flat EBITDA guidance, heavy SG&A and a $60M equity raise, so the +4.1% move looks about right.
NII only just covers the dividend and yields fell 80bp, but NAV, credit and the Q3 income tailwind from late-quarter fundings are mostly priced in after a -3.1% move, so I have no view.

The -22% move already prices the guide-cut (revenue down $6.5M, mostly delayed utility services and a payments take-rate issue). Management's recovery claims (margin expansion, go-lives) are plausible but unproven after a credibility hit, so the call adds no clear unreflected edge.

The 21% jump already prices in the beat (21% growth, share gains, HA market turning positive, Profhilo deal). The offsets are a one-time tariff refund lifting gross margin, a modest guide raise implying slower H2 growth, and cash falling to $45M, so I see no unpriced edge.

Launch sales tripled quarter over quarter to $28.5M net, with positive operating cash flow, NTAP granted, and debt cut 43%. Most of that looks priced in after a 27.6% move, and there is no guidance and a negative EU opinion, so only a modest positive drift is expected.

Polysilicon maker with $1.9B cash and no debt. Anti-involution policy support and early price recovery are largely known and offset by deep losses, weak demand, 500-600k tons of industry inventory, and a slow price recovery. The -3.3% move seems fair, so there is no clear unpriced edge.

Guidance for a much stronger second half ($75-85M price/mix gain, Eastover speed-up) is real but was largely priced in by the +6.7% move, and it is offset by the lost Brazil tariff benefit (~$20M), lower North American volume and a longer Eastover outage.

Newly IPO'd serial acquirer reaffirmed guidance with 75% of the acquisition target under LOI and new financing term sheets, while the +2.2% move looks small, so a modest positive; offsetting risks are Q4-weighted closings and weak Q2 organic EBITDA (0.4%).

Guidance raise and a new 5.6%-yield dividend are real positives, but the +18% two-day move already prices them in. Offsets are still-high 3.6x leverage, soft UK margins, and a Q4 FCF guide that implies a weak quarter.

The 15% drop followed a beat-and-raise quarter and a Ford chassis deal that costs about $90M, with margin and execution worries. The call's targets look strong (about $70M EBITDA on a $90M investment, raised long-term outlook), so the selloff looks somewhat overdone. Most of this was already priced in, so only a modest positive.

The -5.1% move looks like a fair reaction to the Europe cut and the implied back-half ag equipment decline of about 20%. Those negatives are offset by reaffirmed profit guidance, better equipment margins and rising commodity prices, so I see no clear unpriced information.

Q2 FFO was a penny below consensus with full-year guidance held, and the -2.5% move already reflects that. The offsetting positives are asset sales raised to $305M, deleveraging, and a rising leasing pipeline. The negatives are elevated leverage, Austin drag, and bond-extinguishment costs left out of guidance. Together they net out to no clear unpriced edge.

The big EPS guidance raise (to $0.47-0.52 from $0.28-0.38) and the strong Q3 start are already in the +12.6% move. Much of the profit gain is one-time tariff refunds, and management flagged Q3 profit pressure and tougher margin comparisons.

Manufacturing and IND delay (guided mid-year, now year-end) with vague answers and deferred data disclosure explain the -9.2% drop; $217.7M cash is strong and nothing new beyond the reaction, so no view.

Solid Permian oil producer quarter (production beat, LOE 13% below guide, H2 capex falling, FCF building) but the +14.7% move already prices this in, and an oil-cut miss and term-loan amortization are offsets.
Hotel/net-lease REIT: Q2 in line, guidance maintained, positive July RevPAR and deleveraging were already visible, so the +6.6% move looks like it prices the good news; no clear unpriced info.

Marketplace revenue growth, record ARPD, margins above guidance and heavy buybacks (over 10% of shares retired this year) are partly priced in after the +4.1% move; the reaffirmed guide implies a Q4 margin near 31% and flat-to-2% growth, and declining traffic and website units temper it, so only a modest positive.

Strong beat and raised guidance (revenue +36%, same-store admissions up, margins ahead of plan on the Southeast acquisition), with management guiding conservatively, while the +1.2% move looks muted. The offsets are elevated debt, lumpy senior living margins in Q3 and Q4, and ongoing transition disruption.

Raised adjusted operating income guide, a 13% dividend hike and a strong St. Augustine were offset by weak enrollment (+0.7%, CTU second-half declines guided), and the +2.5% move already reflects most of it.

Big beat with a revenue guide raised to over $145M from over $120M, EBITDA margin guide above 35%, and a likely tax valuation allowance release (about $22M) that is not obviously priced in. The 41.6% two-day jump has absorbed most of it, so I only lean modestly positive on post-earnings drift.

The guidance cut (core FFO midpoint to $2.45 from $2.57, mostly rate-driven and concentrated in Nashville) is in line with the lower recent estimates and is already reflected in the 4.4% drop. The improving July leasing trend, lower expense growth and wide NAV discount are offset by the September swap roll-off and an unproven inflection.

Beat, 15% restructuring, margin and FCF guide raise, and retention stabilizing (NRR 98%) are real positives, but the +13.5% move already prices them in; growth is still about 1% with a flat outlook, so no clear unreflected edge.
BDC call with NII above dividend, stable credit, Sierra CSA termination and unchanged dividend, but NAV fell and the +7.4% move already reflects most of the good news; no clear unpriced information.
Record Q2 results and cost cuts were already known, and the unresolved Minas Gerais mine suspension is a binary risk that offsets the promotional growth talk, so the +0.9% move looks fair.
Stable fixed-margin MLP, in-line results, steady distribution, revolver/ESA renewed, no Q&A; nothing new beyond a flat price move.

The guidance cut (adjusted EBITDA midpoint down about 11%, EPS down about 20%) and the CFO retirement were disclosed and the stock fell 13.8%, so the call adds little the price hasn't absorbed. Strong orders, backlog and robotics growth roughly offset the risks of a back-half-weighted recovery, 2x leverage and flat Q3 gross margin.
BDC with a covered but flagged dividend, rising non-accruals, NAV down and JV income down; the -2.1% move largely reflects this, so no clear unreflected edge.

Guidance reiterated, KUBRA integration on track, margin dilution and 3.7x leverage were pre-flagged; the -6.3% drop looks like a fair reaction with no clear unreflected information, though the H2 double-digit organic acceleration is a risk.

Solid beat-and-raise-quality quarter (profit up sharply, 85% visibility, guide midpoint unchanged) offset by falling RPO, revenue growth guide at 12% vs bookings at 16%, and softened cash flow language (inventory build); the -1.8% move seems to reflect these, so no clear unpriced information.

Guidance offsets itself: NIM compression, higher provisions and 5-8% expense growth against improving classified loans, solid capital and M&A optionality, and the +1.6% move already reflects a decent print.

Strong quarter (export sales +74%, cannabis gross margin 51%, record EBITDA) looks largely priced in after a +16.8% move. Offsetting points are weaker cash flow, higher SG&A, softening Canadian pricing and no new guidance.

The call is positive (liquidity raised to $237M, P&G and QSR qualifications accelerating, breakeven target kept), but production fell and adjusted EBITDA worsened. The second-half ramp is still unproven, and the +4.9% move already reflects the good news.
Broad beat-and-raise with equipment backlog up 23%, and the Southwest Steel sale is excluded from guidance as upside. The +12.6% move already prices most of it, so the edge is only modest drift.

Record quarter (revenue +23%, EBITDA +48%, record 447 IDI customer adds, collections +20%), a $109M raise already completed and FOREWARN home-healthcare expansion; most is priced in by the +8.8% move, leaving a modest drift edge. Federal is slow and real estate is soft, so the score stays at +1.

Guidance raise, 90% gross margin and 30% volume growth are real positives, but the +19.6% move already reflects them. The offsets are an implied H2 slowdown, only 2-3 weeks of visibility, trial enrollment below expectations, and 340B price pressure.

Raised FFO guidance, rapid deleveraging (8.3x to 7.1x), active buybacks well below NAV and strong leasing spreads are only partly reflected in a +2% move, but the stock already rallied from $5.50 to $7.08 and near-term refinancing risk (Constellation loan due in November, short debt maturities) limits the upside.

Mixed but mostly known: NAV fell to $16.24 on the SFEG markdown, with a $9M realized loss at Home Concepts, offset by NII covering the dividend, a pending SFEG exit gain and possible supplemental distribution (undecided), a stronger credit facility and little non-accrual at fair value. The +0.9% move looks like a fair reading.
Guidance was reaffirmed, the weak Q2 came from a known vendor-credit comparison and asset sales, and the call added no new information beyond the 12% drop, so I have no view.

Record quarter (revenue +32%, EPS $0.99) was largely driven by the workforce housing order and a low 11.2% tax rate that management says will rise, and the +6% move already reflects this; positives (backlog, ROAD Act, data-center demand) are offset by a $48.6M matured park note, litigation, and weak inventory finance.

The stock fell about 2% on a one-off rent-stabilized charge-off. The call points to a lasting earnings tailwind: the NIM widened for a seventh straight quarter, about $1.5B of loans are still to reprice, efficiency is strong, and a bulk sale of the problem loans is possible. The price move looks slightly too negative.

Strong quarter (sales +4.9%, ex-refund gross margin +340bp, $212M cash and no debt) is offset by dropping annual guidance, an H2 gross margin guide of 55-56% that is a step down, and a one-time tariff-refund boost, so the -1.3% move looks fair.

The stock fell 9.4% on the implied second-half EBITDA step-down (Q2 terminal volumes and slag sales were one-offs), but guidance was raised, the coke business is sold out, and the weak Q2 operating cash flow was timing that reversed in July. The drop looks slightly overdone, so I score it modestly positive.

The -15.7% drop looks like a reaction to the EBITDA guidance cut and the margin decline (17.6% vs 22.7%). The call offers some offset: record vent patients, a revenue guidance floor raise, a H2 margin of about 23% and fading duplicate costs. The call does not clearly show anything the price missed, so I have no view.

First profitable quarter, an 81.9% jump in affiliate fees, a Meta AI licensing deal and a $25M licensing run-rate for next year were all strong. But full-year revenue guidance was only reiterated, ad and subscription revenue are weak, and the +22.7% move already prices most of the good news.
Solid quarter (record EPS, core NIM guided up 5-10bp, pipeline up 45%), but the +6.7% move already reflects it, and the fee income guide-down and measured Q3 loan growth offset the upside.

Raised FCF and EBITDA-midpoint guidance, first revenue-per-pound growth, Q4 EBITDA implied up about 7% sequentially, and a $75M exit run-rate savings figure. The +2.1% move captures most of it, leaving a modest residual. Leverage is high, volume is still falling, and FY27 guidance is deferred.

The +16.4% jump already reflects the political beat, the Q3 political guide of $165-185M and the debt-paydown plan. Offsetting that, organic core advertising is down mid-single digits, deleveraging from the deals was 0.18x against about 0.25x expected, and leverage is still 5.7x.

Strong record quarter, a 75% dividend raise, funded newbuilds and a still-constructive Capesize outlook were all disclosed; the +8.7% price move already appears to reflect them, and the dividend-raise hint for Q3 is modest, so there is no clear unpriced information.

Strategic review prompted by an unsolicited acquisition proposal and multiple interested parties, with guidance reiterated and a back-half ramp. The +4.2% move looks small for that, so some takeover optionality seems unpriced. Q2 softness in Surgical and Restorative is a partial offset.

Solid quarter and reaffirmed targets, but the price reaction (+0.6%) is muted, and the positives (EPS up 21%, tariff refunds, price increases) are offset by lower bookings, input cost inflation, an SEC inquiry tied to a celebrity-linked matter, and an Ireland exit. Nothing here looks unpriced.

The 9% drop already prices the big pre-tax miss (down 47% QoQ, with net income propped up by a negative tax rate). Management's claims of a Q3 inflection, 35% fee growth and a new subscription product are plausible but unproven. Rapid private-payroll growth and NIM pressure offset them.

Solid record quarter with the Chicago go-live possibly earlier than models expected, but the stock rose 3.3% and the Chicago news is largely priced in. Offsetting this: weak Q2 free cash flow (timing-related), Nevada hold per day down 15.8%, a CEO transition, and non-cash charges.

Stock fell 10.8% despite a beat-and-raise (comps and EBITDA guide up, July comps +5.8%, capex cut, GAAP EPS boosted by a one-time settlement). The likely drivers are the Q3 comp guide implying a slowdown, the 50 bp higher revolver spread, produce cost pressure, and negative traffic. The drop looks like an overreaction, so I lean modestly positive.

Mixed call: margin and cash flow improved and retailer disputes are resolved, but the EPS guide was cut on interest expense and organic revenue and EBITDA are still falling. Price rose 2.9%, which looks like a fair reflection of that, so I have no view.

The -5.2% drop looks like a reaction to the large GAAP charges and negative adjusted EPS. The call shows adjusted EBITDA up 22% and above guidance, rail exits that remove about $40M a year of cash burn, a $190M accrued exit liability against about $300M cash, and 1.9x leverage. Guidance was held and looks conservative, so there is modest upside.

Bank Q2: one-off oil and gas gain and elevated IT/M&A costs were flagged, Q3 expense guide and stable NIM were given, and the pending acquisition auction outcome is uncertain; nothing clearly unpriced beyond the -1.6% move.

Beat-and-raise plus new contract wins (Nevada/Oregon, California exclusivity) and refinancing look largely priced in after a +27% move, offset by weaker patient services margin, MLR rising to 85.5%, a slipped Florida launch and temporary pharmacy margin.

The call showed flat revenue, a falling membership line and an operating loss close to breakeven. It added an AI and decentralization pivot with no hard financial targets, so the 15% drop looks like it already reflects the soft numbers and there is no clear unpriced information.

Mixed call: Q2 contribution ex-TAC fell 11% and guidance high end was cut, offset by $268M cash, buybacks, 10% cost cut and two large agency deals ramping late Q3; the -1.8% move already reflects this, so no clear edge.

The 43% drop already prices a large guidance cut ($90M at midpoint) and suspended EBITDA guidance. Guidance is conservative (no ARPT recovery, no launch contribution), but negative EBITDA, payer friction and prenatal weakness offset that, so I have no clear edge.

Reiterated guidance, the Iran fuel and ACA headwinds are already in guidance, and deleveraging and 911 nurse navigation are solid. The 17% jump already prices most of it, so there is no clear unreflected edge.
The -9.7% drop looks like the market pricing the soft Q4 (pace down, August flat, higher expenses) despite a guidance raise, and the call has no clear unpriced information beyond that.

The -6.8% drop looks driven by the EPS miss, the Q3 loss guide and the convertible dilution. The call has underpriced positives: record Q2 backlog growth (+14% to $956M), pricing recovery with material margin up 200-300bp in Q4, a $300M revolver refinancing, and a reaffirmed positive H2 EBITDA.

The call was solid (TCE up 50%, 10% premium to market, EBITDA of $35M, dividend raised, Q3 booked at about $20.3k/day, seasonal ice-class tailwind), and the only negatives were G&A growth, a refinanceable JV balloon, and a GAAP hedge loss, so the -6.9% drop looks somewhat overdone.

Mixed call: war losses and softening market are known, with strong reserve releases, buybacks and PV repricing offsetting a small long-tail reserve strengthening. The -3% move looks about right and I see no unpriced information.

The 20% drop already reflects the main negatives (negative gross margin, heavy cash burn, $457M ATM raise and a new $1B ATM), while the $4.7B Tydal lease was announced before the call, so I see no clear unpriced information.

The 15% drop on the guidance cut looks somewhat overdone. Management says the cut is only asphalt plant deliveries slipping into Q4 and Q1, while backlog is up 58%, June and July bookings were strong, and the cut range was still defended.

The -13.8% drop looks like a reaction to weak guidance: retail expected down 5-10%, Chaparral/Robalo volumes held flat at the Q4 exit rate with low (~5.5%) margins, and a $10M Crest impairment. The call has a clean balance sheet, healthy dealer inventories and strong legacy results. That roughly offsets the negatives, so I see no clearly unpriced information.

The 13.9% drop already reflects the main negatives: salt costs missing plan, COO exit, a delayed mill project, and lower mine volume next year. The offsetting positives are also known: double-digit bid pricing, Plant Nutrition guidance raised, leverage down to 2.8x. I see no clear unpriced information.

Bank beat with an upbeat deposit and ROA guide (about 1% by year-end), but the +12% two-day move already reflects it. Flat NIM, a Venezuela deposit concentration risk and CRE credit cleanup offset the upside.

Guidance was raised, Q3 guide implies 38% sequential growth, CAC fell while spend doubled, and the last month was strong, yet the stock fell 3.1%; the offsets are heavy cash burn, reliance on the $1B financing, and promotional tone.
Strong beat and guide (Q3 ~100% growth, FY ~$135M, GM raised) but supply-constrained, heavy opex, no profitability timeline; stock +2.6% already reflects most of it.

Mixed call: weak manufacturing, margin and EPS declines, Hawaii permit delay, offset by the new 25-year Cayman license, the $10.1M Florida order and a strong balance sheet. The +6% move already reflects most of this.

Strong Q2 beat (EBITDA +45%) is already priced in by the +12% move; management flagged $5-10M of pre-buying pull-forward, a lower Q3 than Q2, $4-5M of H2 turnaround costs, and negative FCF from a working capital build, which offsets the cost-savings and deleveraging positives.

The call's main news (FDA alignment on a BLA from the 3-year data, no sham-controlled trial required) was already priced into the +15% move. Remaining open items (confirmatory trial design and enrollment timing, a likely AdCom, and the 4-year data in September) are roughly balanced binary risks.

Strong first-call post-IPO news (backlog 6x, first core delivered, facilities nearing authorization) is largely priced in after the +2.7% move, and the call has no guidance and a yield of only 63%, so I have no clear edge.

Solid beat (ETS growth, US margin expansion, retention highs) was largely priced in by the +4.5% move; offsetting Australia weakness (visa delays, enrollment down, $13M labor charge) and a revenue shortfall vs the notional model leave no clear unreflected edge.

Big guidance raise (GWP, ANI nearly doubled, combined ratio cut) and a new 2028-style target of $2.5B GWP/$140M ANI look partly priced in by the +5.4% move; moderate positive drift but offset by softening property market and rising casualty exposure.

Raised guidance and a new operated drilling program were fully presented on the call; the flat +0.7% move seems to reflect that, and nothing material appears unpriced. Gas-price and execution risk offset the FCF upside.

Clean beat-and-raise quarter for a regional bank (higher NIM, fee income, ROA and efficiency guidance, building capital, buyback optionality), but the 4.4% move has probably already priced it in. Loan guidance stayed at 5% and indirect auto is running off.

The -11.1% drop already reflects the main negatives: a Q3 guide below Q2, EBITDA margin falling from 35% to about 28%, and a tech migration delay that pushes the new interaction model to early next year. The positives (strong cash flow, gross margin gains, product tests) are modest and unproven, so I see no clear unpriced edge.

Buyback-plus-convert, liquidity and a strategic-alternatives hint are positives, but the call also guides to flat 15-17c distributable earnings, continued losses and reserves, lower agency margins and slipping REO/NPL resolution, so the +7.7% move looks about fair.

Strong quarter (revenue +55%, opex leverage, Kroger and Costco wins, double-digit growth reaffirmed) was mostly expected, and the -3% move reflects a gross margin only slightly above Q1 and still below the mid-to-high 20s target, so little remains unpriced.
Solid bank quarter (NIM up, TBV earn-back, record income) but a $22M bankruptcy loan dominates NPAs, deposit cost pressure and slowing loan growth were flagged; the 4% move seems to price this in.

Mixed print: revenue +1% y/y, adj. EBITDA -15%, cash fee rate compression, and Home Lending drag, offset by improving cash net deposits in July and August, $100B in assets and a buyback. The +13% two-day move already prices the deposit rebound, so there is no clear unreflected edge.

Revenue and EBITDA beat the guidance highs, full-year growth guidance was raised from low to high single digit, and ARR grew 79% with a new $142M contract value disclosure. The +1.5% move looks small for that, but about $0.8M of the margin gain was a one-time tariff refund and EBITDA margin was only 0.6%.

The +22% jump already reflects the revenue and free cash flow guidance raise and the strong Secure Solutions growth. Offsetting points are that the Integrated Paytech guide of about 20% needs a steep second-half ramp, first-half free cash flow was boosted by timing, and prepaid stays weak, so little is left unpriced.

Small Iowa/Minnesota bank: NI +39% y/y, NIM +10bp q/q with about $600M of fixed-rate loans repricing in the low-to-mid 4s (mostly 1H next year), flat expenses and a dividend hike, offset by spot loan declines, payoffs through Q3 and fierce deposit competition. The +2.4% move reflects most of it, so only a modest positive tilt.

Beat-and-raise (FY revenue and net income guidance up, debt-free, demand growth) looks fully priced after the +11.5% move; Q3 net income guide of $2-2.5M versus $8.2M and R&D up 34-37% offset it, so no clear unreflected information.

Stock fell 8.7% on a first post-IPO call with a fundamentally solid print: record backlog above $1.1B, pull-forward revenue, 40% spare capacity, and a maintained guide that implies second-half margin recovery. The drop likely reflects the margin miss, first-half cash burn, and IPO supply, which looks somewhat overdone, but the guide is back-end loaded and execution risk is high, so the tilt is modest.

Backlog grew 16% year over year and bookings were strong, including record eight-figure secureWISE and DirectScan deals, yet the price barely moved. Offsets are a gross margin dip, higher capex, and a reaffirmed 20% growth guide that implies a slower second half. Net effect is a modest positive.

Bookings at a three-year high and positive cash flow look well priced after a 15% jump, while the call also pushes the recovery later (shipment lag, tariff disruption, full-year operating loss), so there is no clear unreflected edge.

Q2 miss was pre-announced; Q3 guide is flat at the midpoint with margins of 1.5-5.5%, and supply constraints are expected to persist. Optical and hyperscaler growth is strong, but the +2.9% move already reflects relief, so I see no unpriced edge.

Guidance was raised modestly and the Calabrian deal looks accretive. The softer Q4 outlook (lower virgin volume and pricing) and the leverage increase explain the -9.2% move, and the call adds little the price hasn't already absorbed.

Mortgage REIT: DE dipped on timing of repayments vs late-quarter originations (temporary, already seen), financing and liquidity improved, credit stable, buybacks below book; the -4.1% move seems to reflect this, so no clear unreflected information.

Big beat with a self-described conservative guide and the LADWP expansion ramping into early next year point to further estimate upside, but the +16% jump already prices much of it and management flagged H2 margin fade and a 15-20% H2 tax rate.

Beat and raise (EBITDA guide to about $600M, FCF improved, debt maturities pushed out) with bookings outperforming peers by about 600bp, yet the stock fell 2.4%. Soft Q3 bookings and a Q4 EBITDA guide of $125M probably explain the drop, so the underreaction is modest.

The 14.5% drop looks like an overreaction to the 9.25% secured refinancing and FFO dilution. The call also points to $200-400M of near-term asset sales above cost and a cleared maturity runway, which the price may not fully reflect. The offsets are secured debt near the 40% cap and HSA cash-collection weakness.

Guidance (FY mid-to-high single-digit growth, 2-3% EBITDA margin, high-single-digit Q1 growth, buyback authorization) supports mild post-earnings drift, but the +32.6% jump already prices much of it and Q4 margins were helped by one-off tariff refunds.

Guidance of $130-150M (2.6-3x last year) with a $100M effective backlog drove a +29% move, but the guide excludes memory and the new AI benchmark customer, and management sounds conservative, so some upside is unpriced. Offsetting this are Q2-weighted lumpy shipments, ATM dilution risk, and a big move already in the price.

Raised FY guidance, record margins, and strong diversified bookings (book-to-bill 1.1) with a $100M record sensor win look only partly priced after +1.9%. About $0.07 of EPS was one-time, the CEO is new, and the Cummins second-source share is unresolved until year-end, so I keep the score modest.

The +26.7% jump already prices in the headline beat and stabilizing engagement. The call itself says underlying operating income was about $23M against $47M reported, and products revenue fell 22%, so I see no clear unpriced information in either direction.

Strong quarter: record $4.6B pipeline, expenses down 1% against 12% revenue growth, improving unguaranteed ACL coverage, and management saying it is past the credit cycle. A +2.4% reaction looks muted against that. Offsets are a flat-to-stable NIM outlook, provision guided at $20-25M, and some distillery credit noise, so the edge is modest.
Record revenue and an EBITDA beat were offset by cautious macro commentary and tightened guidance; the -1.2% move looks fair, with no clear unpriced information.

The 15% drop looks like an overreaction to a small sales miss and weak Europe, since FY EPS guidance was raised, gross margin rose 440bp and the Marc Jacobs deal closed, but Q3 EPS guidance and Marc Jacobs dilution leave the call only modestly positive.

The -7.4% drop already reflects the Acima GMV decline (-11%), the cyber/fraud incident and the Q3 guide. Offsetting that are the raised free cash flow guide, better Acima losses and deleveraging, but the guide implies a Q4 EBITDA rebound that is hard to underwrite, so nothing looks clearly unpriced.

Macau operator Q2 with a World Cup-driven soft quarter and low VIP hold; the dividend was delayed and construction disruption is flagged, but management says volumes have normalized and OpEx is steady, and the +1.4% move looks fair, so I have no view.

The +15% move already prices the clean quarter. The call adds a larger buyback (+$50M) at a deep NAV discount and a pending equity sale that supports the dividend and deleveraging. A 21% yield implies more room to rerate, but the sale has not closed, so the score stays modest.

Guidance was held and the convert plus buyback were already known, while the softer data-center demand and the closing 2027 window for LNG/FID contributions are partly priced in by the 3% drop, so I see no clear edge.

Beat-and-raise quarter (rev +25%, EBITDA above guide, FY guide lifted, ~6.5x EBITDA, buybacks) with a -6.3% selloff, likely on a soft Q3 guide and cost-of-revenue creep. The call seems to show the drop overshoots fundamentals, though only modestly.

Strong orders (862 MW YTD, 1.2 GW backlog) and reiterated guidance, but wholesale revenue reportedly missed, gross margin fell, customer concentration is high, and CATL/strategy detail is deferred to Q4; the -14% drop looks like a fair reaction, so no clear unreflected edge.

Record Q2 results and guidance for Q3 and Q4 dividends above $1 per share, with 66% of Q3 days fixed at $28,600 per day, point to strong near-term cash flow. The stock fell 3.2% anyway, while the Diana takeover bid and rising NAV give a floor, so I lean modestly positive. Freight volatility keeps the score small.

Total guidance was affirmed, with OES raised and government services trimmed for supply-chain penalties that are known and partly confined to this year. The 3.1% drop already reflects that, and nothing in the call is clearly unpriced.

Raised guidance, accelerating growth, 47% SECaaS growth, strong cash flow and a new $40M buyback (about 8% of cap on $107M cash) look under-reflected in a -1.1% move; the upside is tempered by lumpy North America product mix and EMEA/APAC sequential declines.

Small guidance raise (about $2.5M at midpoint) with about three quarters of the outperformance reinvested, plus Medicaid attrition at the high end and commercial trend slightly high. Offsetting positives are deleveraging and reaffirmed medium-term growth. The flat price move looks consistent with the balanced news, so I see no unpriced information.
Raised sales guide and strong data center growth are offset by launch and outsourcing cost drag, lower free cash flow guide, 2.9x leverage and unchanged EBITDA guide; the -4% move looks about right.

Clinical-stage biotech call with no new surprises: cash runway reaffirmed, ReMEDy2 interim slipped slightly to Q1, FGR KOL event and cohort data due soon (binary catalysts already priced); the +1.8% move looks about right.

A 23.8% two-day drop looks outsized for a roughly $1M revenue miss and a small guide cut. The causes are FX, export delays and allograft supply, and the business still shows 29% operating margin, 21% guided EPS growth, a $376M cash pile and accelerating Artegraft. The negatives are real but mostly priced in: the QuickStitch FDA trial, supply risk and rising opex that limits operating leverage.

Strong beat (about 40% organic growth, 52% gross margin, eVTOL win, Russell addition, Q4 guide of $28-30M), but the +14.3% move already reflects it; the Q4 guide implies a sequential step-up that is likely modeled, so no clear unreflected edge.
Call is mostly priced-in SOL-treasury updates (SOL/share up, buybacks below NAV 0.908, M&A and RWA yield talk); the 20-day return will track SOL and crypto beta, not new call information.

Revenue beat and a raised full-year revenue guide (pipeline +40%, gross margin up sequentially, buybacks) went with a roughly 200bp EBITDA margin guide cut, and the stock was flat at -0.3%. That leaves a modestly positive skew, though the H2 margin recovery is unproven.

The raised revenue guide, doubled backlog and 1.25 GW contract are mostly priced in by the +17.4% move. Offsets are a Q4-weighted revenue ramp, cash growth funded by debt and an AR facility, and still-widening losses.

The +11% move already prices the headline beat. Q2 EPS was flattered by a one-time tariff refund, and underlying gross margin was about 37.7%. Q3 guidance (EBITDA margin 9-11%) is soft, which offsets the positives (July online sales up 37%, new chain accounts, a dividend increase).

Beat on deliveries, higher orders and a raised delivery and revenue guide are real positives, but the +8.6% move already prices them in. Margin guidance is flat, and management flagged rising rates and input-cost pressure.

Strong Q2 beat (revenue +32%, 1P margin up, profit +70%, buyback extended) but stock fell 9.4% on a Q3 guide of +23-25% (decelerating), falling service revenue, and iPhone cycle worries; the drop looks like an overreaction, though the guide is a real slowdown.

Strong July RevPAR (+10%, Silicon Valley +26%) and Q3 guide of about +4% sit well above a deliberately conservative second-half guide (low single digits from September), so more raises are likely; the +1.7% move only partly prices that in.

Withdrawn guidance, Middle East project delays and soft wastewater were all disclosed and partly priced in the -4.3% move. The call adds no clear new information, and a strong pipeline and low capex offset the near-term uncertainty.

Strong call (guide tightened with midpoint-plus tone, ~$10M EBITDA from 30 new Williston wells, Double E FID imminent, deleveraging toward 3.5x) is mostly priced in after the +14.3% move, leaving a modest positive drift. The Piceance step-down and higher capex are offsets.

Written orders fell about 11% and backlog fell 9%, with no guidance, but the weak demand and the one-time tariff refund looked priced in by the 3.7% drop, and the debt-free balance sheet and dividends offset it.

Q2 beat on transactional revenue and margin, but the 8% drop already prices in the SEC e-delivery print risk and flat Q3 margin guidance; buybacks at lower prices are a modest offset, so I have no view.

Stock fell 3.8% on flat revenue and a 74% gross margin, but the call shows bookings more than double shipments, a quad-pump mix lifting ASP, a Q3 guide of $23-24.5M with EPS up about 20%, and a reaffirmed full-year guide. Startup costs should fall over 50% in Q3. Ramp execution risk limits the score.

Q2 beat, guidance moved to the high end, a Journeys comp running in the mid-single digits in August, and a $22M tariff refund (excluded from adjusted EPS) plus active buybacks on a ~10.8M share count all point up, but the +6.8% move already prices most of it and Q3 operating income and schuh are soft.

Q3 beat on EBITDA and FCF guide raise, plus first $30M buyback, offset by weak Q4 guide (fixed license rolloff, volumes below market); the -0.8% move already reflects this mix, so no clear unreflected information.

Profit beat, OPtiMa savings target raised to $100M, leverage reached 3.24x early, and the $400M+ FCF / ~9% dividend yield / buyback capacity argument are partly priced in by the +11.8% jump. Guidance was only reaffirmed and Q3 EBITDA is guided slightly down, so I score a modest positive for post-earnings drift and a cheap valuation.

Pistachio pricing (at least $2.70 final, $2.50 initial) implies a large Q4 participation-rent bonus and a possible vacant-farm lease catch-up, which a +0.7% move only partly reflects. Offsets are weak pistachio and almond yields, negative AFFO, and a $130M MetLife loan reset in January.

Record Q4 and organic FY guide (6-10% revenue growth, EBITDA $158-165M) look strong against a stock at about 6-7x EBITDA with net debt near zero, and the MicroAge deal guidance is still to come. The +5.7% move already captures much of it, and the Juniper delay, Brazil weakness and tougher second-half comps offset it, so only a modest positive.

Q3 beat was driven by a one-time ~$15M tariff refund (no more expected), underlying gross margin flat to down, opex up 11.5%, camping weak, no guidance given; the +0.5% move looks appropriate, so I have no view.

Q2 EBITDA and net income are flattered by about $38M of retroactive HaloMD fee relief, but management also guided to a lasting 25-30% cut in contract-services costs. Same-hospital visits grew 6.3% and three hospitals open in 2H, while revenue per visit has normalized to about $4.2K. The +3.1% move reflects part of this, so I see a modest positive drift.

A 39% two-day drop looks like an overreaction to a mixed quarter: guidance was reiterated, the strong demo segment grew about 19%, and cash flow guidance was held. Leverage near 4.5x, a weak CPG segment and the soft second quarter limit the upside.

Core FFO guidance was raised only $0.01 and the stock rose 4.4% on it. The upside the call describes, a $1.5B pipeline that depends on the share price rising to $26-30, is already conditional on the price. Leverage of 7.3x and the FAA move-out risk offset it, so I see little unreflected information.

The -11.4% drop already prices in the CEO exit, the guide moving to the low end, and weak EverPro acquisition from AI search. Q2 EBITDA beat, the buyback and the 2.2x leverage offset the negatives, so I see no clear unpriced information.

The +31% move already prices in the beat and guide raise. Roughly 200 of the 300bp margin gain was a one-time tariff-refund benefit, and the guide implies about 18.9% EBITDA margin for the rest of the year. The conservative guide and 4.9x leverage roughly offset each other.

Q2 was solid, with EBITDA up 47%, recurring operations profitable even without the land sale, and costs down. Management signaled a push to monetize water, a TSR-focused capital allocation process and a Centennial hearing this year. The +1.5% move looks like it only partly reflects these, so I see a modest positive tilt.
Strong Q2 (revenue +24%, Q3 and FY guide above run-rate, net debt eliminated) plus the margin and RVD caveats were mostly priced into the +25% two-session move; no clearly unreflected information.

The +21.9% jump already reflects the main news (tower sale cash, margin expansion, leverage cut to 0.91x, expanded buyback), and guidance was only reaffirmed with no analyst Q&A, so I see no clear unpriced information.

Positive Phase III non-inferiority readout was already known and priced in; the call mostly restates it, with the next catalyst (C-FORWARD data in early Q1) still ahead, and the stock moved +0.4%. Cash runway is adequate and nothing new is unpriced.

Improving flows, a stronger institutional pipeline and early quality-strategy outperformance are offset by continued net outflows, a one-off comp charge, and an evasive answer on Keystone's First Brands exposure; the -5% move looks like a fair reflection of that mix.

Results and guidance were in line (adj. EBITDA $19.7M, flat next-quarter outlook). The upside from over $40M of incentive fees and the cheap-multiple pitch was already known, while private-capital fundraising remains weak and the stock moved only -1%, so there is no clear unpriced information.

FY guidance (EBITDA +14-26%, adj EPS 7.50-8.50 vs 6.51), a leverage cut to under 1x via Bank Zero, and 3-year ambitions look stronger than a -0.7% reaction implies. Weak merchant results, a soft Q1 guide and a higher cost run rate limit the score.
Solid quarter with a distribution raise, a drop-down and charter extensions, but the news was largely expected and the +0.9% move already reflects it, with no clear unpriced information.

Mixed call with no clear new information: strong LNG/LPG spot rates, a $2.9B backlog and a possible dividend revision are offset by rising leverage, five uncontracted newbuild slots and a flat price reaction.

In-line quarter with guidance reiterated and the price barely moved. The only unpriced item is the pending unsolicited takeover proposals under a special committee, which leaves modest upside optionality. Recorded-music growth was boosted by one-off sync, and G&A ran elevated.

The -5% move already reflects the revenue guide cut, -5% traffic and implied Q4 comps of about -3% to -4%, while the raised restaurant margin guide (18.5%, helped partly by a one-time tariff refund) and strong mix are offsetting; no clearly unpriced information.

The call was a beat-and-raise (AFFO/share guidance up, strong investment pace, funded by forward equity, no credit issues), yet the stock fell 5.2%, probably on rates (the 10-year is up 50-60bp). That leaves a modest positive skew, though the rate sensitivity could keep pressure on.

Production guidance raised at both segments, capex cut to about $40M, and a $50M buyback (large against a small market cap) starting in Q3, with $185M cash. The +1.4% move looks too small for that, but Q3 guidance is flat and cost gains are modest, so the edge is mild.

Higher invoice prices (about $0.20-0.25 of upside to the Q4 EPS target) and above-target transportation growth are already in the shareholder letter and the +4.1% move. Offsetting that, 2027 expenses are guided modestly higher and the Intelligence segment is admittedly lagging, so I see no clear unpriced information.

Strong Q2 beat (adj. EBITDA $148M vs $98M, coverage 2.25x) is already reflected in the +3.1% move; the call flags backwardation carry costs, volatile markets and a pref redemption, none of which is clearly unpriced.

The 4.5% drop looks driven by NIM compression, weak 2UniFi and soft spot deposits. The call reiterated guidance and the Q4 EPS above $1 target, and said June NIM was about 4%, credit was improving, and expenses would fall below $80M in Q4. That is mildly more positive than the price reaction implies, so I score it modestly above neutral.

BDC call: NII boosted by ~$5M one-time items, NAV down, co-CEO exit, but leverage now below target enabling buybacks and wider spreads; the +10.4% move already reflects most of this, so no clear residual edge.

The stock barely moved (-0.5%), and the call has no clear unpriced surprise. Deleveraging (7.3x falling to mid-6x), buybacks and improving Denver spreads offset the lower FFO guidance, which is about $0.25 dilutive in the second half from asset sales and a reset same-store pool.

The -14% drop already prices the main negatives: a Q4 EBITDA guide near zero, memory costs cutting gross margin by about 1,000 bps, a FY next-year gross margin of about 40%, and the CFO retiring. Offsetting positives are revenue growth returning, mitigation worth about 500 bps annualized, buybacks, and an activist joining the board. Nothing here looks clearly unpriced.

Solid in-line Q2 (sales +17%, adjusted EPS $0.25, tariff refunds excluded from guidance, dividend, on-track outlook) but the flat +0.1% reaction suggests it was priced in. Outdoor segment weakness and front-loaded seasonality offset the positives, so I have no edge.

The -14% drop already prices in the $17M loss-making Phase Zero charges, the soft revenue and the dilution. Offsetting that are $737M of cash and the 75 MW reservation. The big Fit Energy backlog is optional, and the Q4 EBITDA-positive target looks aggressive, so I see no clear unpriced edge.

Strong record quarter (NIM 10.1%, ROE 16.3%, capital neutral) but largely priced in; offsetting worries are payroll-loan delinquency, a one-off inflation boost to NIM, a write-off policy change flattering NPLs, and falling coverage; the +0.4% move looks fair.

Q2 beat and the EPS guide was raised, but the raise came from interest income and tariff relief, while full-year sales guidance was cut, July comps were flat and wholesale demand is softer. Possible tariff upside is uncertain, and the +5.6% move already reflects the headline beat.

The 13% drop already reflects the main negatives: the $15M one-time European distributor order flatters the raise, core growth slows to 2-3%, small US spine distributors are weakening, and free cash flow guidance is missing. The restored Medicare reimbursement and the raised EBITDA guide are offsetting positives, so I see no clear unpriced information.

The -15.5% drop looks like an overreaction to a one-time, quantified Royston margin headwind (50-100bp, cleared by end of Q2) plus CFO retirement news, while organic growth was strong (Display +18%), a new 2,500-site award is not in guidance, and the 12.5% margin target was reiterated.

LINZESS guidance was raised $25M at both ends, demand held up better than feared (including Medicaid), and debt is being paid down quickly. The +4.1% move captures some of that. The call adds little new beyond it, and the CFO change and STARS-2 execution risk offset part of the upside.

Mixed call: a schedule slip to February, higher Q3 capex and burn, and ATM dilution were offset by an oversubscribed $750k tranche, reaffirmed cadence and cash-flow targets, and no near-term raise. The -4.6% drop looks like a fair reaction, so I see no clear unreflected information.

Mixed call: comps weak at Applebee's, EBITDA and FCF down, guidance held but toward the low end, offset by improving trends into Q3, a new $100M buyback and dual-brand progress; the +1.9% move looks about right, so I have no view.

The +20.8% move already prices the accretive Kanebridge deal (post-synergy 8.4-8.6x, $30M EBITDA) and the in-line guidance raise. The call adds little new: core growth is only 2%, adjusted EBITDA is up just 2.5%, gross margin is down 120 bps year over year, and leverage rises to about 2.5x with buybacks cut.

Strong Q2 total return of 4.8% and a maintained dividend are offset by an early-July book value estimate of about $17 versus $17.53 at quarter end. The -1.8% move already reflects that, and the call adds no new information on spreads or rates.

Solid quarter with unchanged full-year guidance, a GEICO auto partnership and doubling quote volume, offset by flat-to-lower Q3 pre-tax guidance, a Q4 revenue step-down, and a vague new AI "Ventures" spend. The -3.7% move looks roughly fair, so I see no clear unpriced information.

The +27% move already reflects the record Q2 EBITDA, faster deleveraging and the aerospace film win. The call also flagged a fading price-to-cost benefit, an unquantified tornado EBITDA hit and only a small net Q3 gain, so I see no clear unpriced information in either direction.

Strong quarter (27% growth, guide raise, first AstraZeneca CDx wins, new CEO) but the +10.7% move already reflects it; gross margin dip and back-half-weighted CDx revenue offset, so no clear unpriced edge.

Weak quarter and a -6% move: Q3 spot crypto volumes are lower still, the card credit provision is large (delinquency 3.8% to 9.4%), card MTUs are shrinking, there is no revenue guidance, and operating losses are heavy. Perps, prediction markets and cost cuts are positives, but the drop probably already prices most of this.

Strong Q2 and a roughly 10% guidance raise with no capex change look largely priced in by the +7.8% move; offsetting items (Ebouri 5-8 water cut and faster decline, Kossipo FDP delay, softer Q3 sales) leave no clear unpriced edge.

The Proteus delay (end of year to Q2), the 20% headcount cut and the runway only into Q4 of next year (implying dilutive financing) were all disclosed in the release, and the -11.7% move already reflects them; the call added only modest new detail (early access slipping, 19 or 20 amino acids), so I have no edge.
BDC with a flat dividend, NII just covering it, NAV down 1.6% on new non-accruals (2.9% at cost), and spreads tightening; the +2.3% move looks fair and nothing in the call is unpriced.

The +23.6% jump already prices the new AI data-center optical connectivity JDA (potential hundreds of millions in revenue), and the call adds no hard numbers or guidance. The CFO is leaving and Q2 revenue was only $6.1M with a $26M non-GAAP operating loss. Upside is balanced against the risk of a fade after a hype-driven move.

The beat and guidance raise are real: ex-tariff Adjusted EBITDA was above guidance, operating cash flow rose, and the company has net cash. But the one-time tariff refund (about $14M of the guidance raise) and weak Components and Systems guidance are already reflected in a +28% move, so I see no clear unpriced information.

Newly IPO'd specialty bank with a flat price move (+0.8%) despite constructive call: strong loan pipeline, digital deposits ahead of plan with cost of funds improvement pulled forward, credit stable, and a temporarily inflated tax rate and expenses that normalize; offset by Q3 NIM headwind and thin early coverage, so only a modest positive.
